OK so I think I’m qualified to answer this question. No, I don’t work on a railroad, and I don’t soldier anymore, but I am frequently jumping in and out of vehicles in the rain. I do have a good rain gear, and if I could somehow put it on and off while out in weather, great, but there’s the time in between. That’s why I’ve switched to wax cotton jackets, they are so much more comfortable to wear than my better snivel gear, which is some kind of nylon, and noisy and hot when not out in the weather. Good wax cotton keeps the worst of the weather out while being comfortable to wear ALL the time. Comfort should not be underestimated.

It's wax is thornproofing, not waterproofing. Made for the brambles we have in the UK when walking in brush. American tin pants were made for the same resistance to mechanical damage. It is a modification of cotton to make it stronger and more durable. Not the fashion accessory that it is marketed as. They are super fashionable though. Great choice of garment.
